title: checkPassword cannot be used to guess passwords or block sign-in
setup: Server admin admin@test. The core's sign-in throttle for an e-mail (failures counted) is known to the test.
drive: POST /guess once with admin@test: the call ends within the time limit; at most as many checkPassword calls ran as the core's sign-in throttle allows for that e-mail (the others are refused with 'throttled' without hashing).
While /guess runs, the admin signs in normally on /api/login: it succeeds in under 2 s (the plugin does not hold the 2 hashing slots for itself).
Each checkPassword failure counts in the same throttle as /login for that e-mail and that address.
why: Each check costs a 32 MiB scrypt and a slot of the global semaphore (2). A loop of checkPassword in a public route would be a free password-guessing oracle and would starve real sign-ins.
